items.title: For a function between sets the kernel relation is effective

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Proposition 10.1.9 at source lines 385-389: for any function f:A->B between sets, the relation ker(f,x,y) defined as f(x)=f(y) is effective. The author's proof (source lines 391-417) runs on the comparison map c_f(a) = (f(a), |a,refl|) into the image and on the kernel pair of that map. The two identifications that have to be carried out are not routine: the type c_f(x)=c_f(y) is first rewritten as a sum over p:f(x)=f(y) with a transported truncation on each side, and the collapse of that sum uses the fact that the fibre of f is a mere proposition; one then has to see that the resulting equivalence of kernel pairs is precisely effectivity. The statement records only the relation and the conclusion, and neither the comparison map nor the mere-proposition step appears in it.
